featured_reviews.name: Ameeta mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Warning Based on Our Experience.

I am writing this review with a heavy heart, as we truly hoped for a great partnership with AV Arch & Design Studio for our new office fit-out in Malad. Unfortunately, our experience was deeply disappointing and financially stressful. I feel compelled to share our story so others can avoid the same pitfalls.

Our journey with them started promisingly. Their initial presentation showed stunning projects, and Vinay, who handles the client meetings, was very persuasive. However, cracks began to show almost immediately after we signed the agreement and made the first payment.

The major issues we faced:

Constant Delays & Ghosting: The project timeline they promised was a fantasy. Deadlines for drawings, material approvals, and site work were consistently missed. Getting a response from the team became a weekly struggle. Calls would go unanswered for days, and messages on WhatsApp were often left on "read." The lack of basic communication and project management was incredibly frustrating for a commercial project where time is money.

The "Bait and Switch" on Quality: This was our biggest shock. In the meetings, we were shown samples of high-quality laminates, sturdy hardware, and specific branded sanitaryware. What started arriving on-site was noticeably inferior. The laminate finish was different and felt cheaper, the door handles were lightweight and felt flimsy compared to the samples, and several tiles had slight colour variations, suggesting they were from different, possibly leftover, batches. When confronted, we were given excuses about "material unavailability" or told, "This is the same grade, just from a different lot." It felt like a classic bait-and-switch.

Unprofessional Site Execution: The quality of workmanship was inconsistent. We noticed uneven plastering, poorly aligned ceiling panels, and paintwork that was patchy in corners. The carpenters on site seemed to be working without detailed drawings, leading to errors that had to be corrected. There was no dedicated, knowledgeable project manager present to ensure quality control. The feeling was that once the payment was released for a phase, their attention and care dropped significantly.

Surprise Costs & Rigid Contracts: The initial quote seemed competitive, but we encountered multiple "additional charges" that weren't adequately explained during planning. For example, minor electrical changes or extra points were billed at a premium rate. The contract heavily favoured them and made it very difficult to address these issues without halting the entire project.

The Portfolio Question (A Later Discovery): After our project ended, a business associate mentioned that one of the office designs AV Arch & Design showed us as "their work" looked remarkably similar to a project done by another well-known firm in Andheri. We did a reverse image search on some pictures from their social media and website, and to our dismay, found matches on other architects' portfolios. We cannot say for sure if all their work is misrepresented, but this discovery shattered our remaining trust completely.

In the end, we had a space that looked okay from a distance but lacked the finesse and quality we paid for. The stress, constant follow-ups, and feeling of being misled were not worth it. What should have been an exciting process turned into a full-time job of monitoring and arguing.

My honest advice:
Please, do your homework. Get everything in writing—exact material brands, codes, and quantities. Don't just go by glossy pictures; try to visit a current site of theirs (not just a completed one they show you) and speak to past clients privately if you can. Most importantly, trust your gut. If communication is poor during the sales stage, it will only get worse later.

There are many good professionals in Mumbai. We learned the hard way that a smooth talk and a low quote are not worth the headache of poor execution and compromised quality. We regret hiring AV Arch & Design Studio and cannot recommend them.
